_note: Action cards for Survive the Sol. effects: power / life / rad = the 3 bars, score = science points, morale = crew mood, plant = space plant health. Every card has a cost. 'icon' is a name from js/icons.js. 'solar': true means the card gives less power in the lunar night or a dust storm. 'shelter': true protects the crew from the next solar flare (halves the hit).

cards.title: Build a shield wall
cards.desc: Pile soil around the base.
cards.science: Thick layers of Moon or Mars soil (regolith) can block a lot of radiation. NASA studies using it to cover bases.

cards.title: Make a water wall
cards.desc: Move water tanks around the beds.
cards.science: Water is very good at stopping radiation, so space bases can keep their water in the walls.

cards.title: Get the storm shelter ready
cards.desc: Next solar storm hits only half as hard.
cards.science: On NASA's Orion spacecraft, astronauts can build a small shelter out of supply bags during a solar storm.

cards.title: Check radiation badges
cards.desc: Find the safest rooms to work in.
cards.science: Astronauts wear small radiation meters called dosimeters to keep track of their radiation dose.

cards.title: Fix the solar panels
cards.desc: A spacewalk to repair panels.
cards.science: The International Space Station gets its electricity from huge solar arrays.

cards.title: Sweep dust off panels
cards.desc: Clean panels give more power.
cards.science: The Mars rovers Spirit and Opportunity got extra power when wind blew dust off their solar panels.

cards.title: Start the small nuclear generator
cards.desc: Lots of power, day and night.
cards.science: In 2018 NASA's Kilopower (KRUSTY) test showed a small nuclear reactor could one day power a base on the Moon or Mars.

cards.title: Turn off extra lights
cards.desc: Save power, but the crew feels gloomy.
cards.science: Spacecraft switch off machines they do not need, so the power lasts longer.

cards.title: Grow vegetables
cards.desc: Fresh food and a happy plant.
cards.science: Astronauts grow lettuce on the ISS in a small plant chamber called Veggie.

cards.title: Recycle water
cards.desc: Clean used water to drink again.
cards.science: The ISS recycles about 98% of its water, even water from sweat and urine!

cards.title: Make oxygen from water
cards.desc: Split water into air to breathe.
cards.science: On the ISS, a machine uses electricity to split water into oxygen (to breathe) and hydrogen.

cards.title: Fix the air filter
cards.desc: Remove bad air (carbon dioxide).
cards.science: The ISS has machines that pull carbon dioxide, the gas we breathe out, from the cabin air.

cards.title: Dig for ice in a dark crater
cards.desc: Ice gives water, but it is far away.
cards.science: Water ice is hidden in very cold, dark craters near the Moon's south pole.

cards.title: Make oxygen from Mars air
cards.desc: Turn carbon dioxide into oxygen.
cards.science: NASA's MOXIE machine on the Perseverance rover made real oxygen from the thin Mars air.

cards.title: Run a science experiment
cards.desc: Learn new things for Earth.
cards.science: Astronauts on the ISS have done thousands of science experiments since 2000.

cards.title: Send the rover to explore
cards.desc: Find cool rocks for science.
cards.science: NASA's Perseverance rover collects rock samples on Mars so scientists can study them.

cards.title: Rest the crew
cards.desc: Happy crew, but no work done.
cards.science: ISS astronauts have about 8.5 hours for sleep in their daily plan.

cards.title: Exercise time
cards.desc: Strong bodies, but more food and air used.
cards.science: ISS astronauts exercise about 2 hours every day to keep their bones and muscles strong.

cards.title: Call family on Earth
cards.desc: Big smiles, but the radio uses power.
cards.science: Radio signals take only about 1.3 seconds to travel from the Moon to Earth.

cards.title: Record a video for Earth
cards.desc: Family will see it many minutes later.
cards.science: A message between Mars and Earth takes about 3 to 22 minutes one way, so live calls are impossible.

cards.title: Health check-up
cards.desc: Crew feels cared for, uses supplies.
cards.science: ISS astronauts do their own medical tests, like ultrasound scans, with help from doctors on Earth.
